first_impression.reaction: Googled 'get married in new zealand' on the train. First line is a straight yes, it's dated November 2026, and the Key Takeaways give me the 3 working days and 3 months rule. That's what I came for. But the whole page is pitched at Australians, and I'm in Singapore, so I'm half working out what applies to me. Every time money comes up it's 'a fee applies'. Bookmarked for the licence steps, not more than that.

journey.quote: Yes, you can get married in New Zealand as Australians, and you do not need to be New Zealand citizens: visitors to New Zealand can marry there.
journey.reaction: Answer in the very first line. Love that. And 'visitors can marry there' covers me too, even though it says Australians.

journey.quote: There is a form to sign before you leave Australia, a registry office to visit after you land, and a certificate to prepare for home.
journey.reaction: Leave Australia, certificate for home. I'm not leaving Australia. Is the form the same if I'm flying from Singapore? I'm guessing yes but I have to guess.

journey.quote: This guide takes each step in the order you will meet it, with the rules as at November 2026.
journey.reaction: Dated. Good, I know it's current.

journey.quote: The licence must be in place at least 3 working days before the wedding, lasts 3 months, and only covers the venues you name on it, so name a back-up.
journey.reaction: This is the screenshot. Real numbers plus a tip I wouldn't have known about the back-up venue.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in New Zealand?
journey.quote: Before the wedding you apply for a marriage licence, which confirms it is legal for you to marry, and a fee applies.
journey.reaction: How much though? Just tell me roughly how much it costs.

journey.section: Before you fly: entry and documents
journey.quote: You can drive for up to 12 months on an Australian driver's licence.
journey.reaction: Driving, bar ID, Medicare, consulates. None of this is the marriage bit and none of it applies to me. Scrolled past a lot to get to the licence steps.

journey.quote: Signing the declaration is not the wedding ceremony: you are declaring that you are legally allowed to marry and that you have been truthful on the form.
journey.reaction: Clear. I'd have been confused by 'registry office' otherwise. It also answers my 'do we fly twice' worry: no, just a visit after landing.

journey.quote: Lodges, vineyard estates and private homes are the usual settings for a New Zealand wedding at this level, and each prices differently.
journey.reaction: At what level? Nothing before this says how big or fancy. Then it asks about a private security team. Not me.

journey.quote: No. You need 2 witnesses who understand what is happening, can clearly identify you both and are satisfied you both consent.
journey.reaction: Direct answer first. The FAQ is good, short and matches what I'd type.

journey.section: Plan your New Zealand wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor stays with you from start to finish, works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: AUD again. Australian company. Fine, not for me right now.

turn_offs_found.why: 'At this level' refers to nothing earlier on the page, and the private security question that follows assumes a high-profile wedding. A normal searcher feels it's written for someone else.

turn_offs_found.quote: You can drive for up to 12 months on an Australian driver's licence.
turn_offs_found.why: The 'Before you fly' section spends several paragraphs on driving, bar ID, Medicare and consulates before the licence steps. On a phone that's a long scroll past things that aren't the answer I came for.

turn_offs_found.quote: Before the wedding you apply for a marriage licence, which confirms it is legal for you to marry, and a fee applies.
turn_offs_found.why: Cost is the first follow-up question and the page repeatedly says 'a fee applies' with no figure or even a pointer to where the current fee is listed.

turn_offs_found.quote: There is a form to sign before you leave Australia, a registry office to visit after you land, and a certificate to prepare for home.
turn_offs_found.why: The framing is Australia-only throughout, so a non-Australian searcher has to guess which steps still apply.

would_share_with: My partner: the Key Takeaways and the 'Applying from Australia' section, as screenshots

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [talk to Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=get-married-in-new-zealand&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I got the steps I came for. I don't know this brand, it quotes in AUD and is aimed at Australians, and I'm nowhere near choosing a planner. Bookmark, not enquiry.

top_3_changes: Fix the 'Venues and planning' opener: drop or explain 'at this level', and make the private security question an optional extra rather than a default.
Shorten 'Before you fly' or move the driving, bar ID, Medicare and consulate notes below the licence steps (or add a jump link) so the licence answer comes sooner on mobile.

Where the page says 'a fee applies', link to where the current official fee is published, and add one line saying the licence process (BDM 58, registry visit) is the same for visitors from any country if the source supports it.
